title: Number, Isness & Theology Atlas v0.1
description: Closed release-specific schema for the immutable reviewed atlas. Validation establishes exact parsed-value conformance, not byte identity, theological truth, or authority.
$comment: This schema cannot recompute the semantic digest or authenticate source availability. Raw bytes, duplicate-key and UTF-8 handling, semantic integrity, mathematical soundness, historical or translation fidelity, theological truth, and authority require independent verification.

verification_note.const: The revision-pinned GitHub URL inherited by predecessor atlases returned 404 on 2026-08-14. This atlas makes no public-access claim; the digest was checked against the repository-local path and revision object.

question.const: How can changes in mathematical expression illuminate number, zero, symmetry, being, negation, creation, God-language, and religious compatibility without turning analogy into proof?

intended_use.const: Read-only education, typed question design, source comparison, and bounded opt-in philosophical reflection.

excluded_use.const: No proof or disproof of God, revelation, creation doctrine, religious truth, cosmic purpose, or karma; no religion, culture, community, or person ranking; no persuasion, governance, invocation, event, receipt, or action.

method.const: Keep formal mathematics, historical scholarship, source attribution, school-specific theology, metaphysical proposal, comparative relation, and analogy in separate registers; every bridge records what it does not transfer.

central_boundary.const: A mathematical structure can sharpen the form of a question. It does not supply the theological premises, translation, interpretation, soundness, actuality, or authority required to answer that question.

rule.const: Every reviewed claim has a discourse register, review target, review status, support descriptors, and source scope. Source attribution can be supported without the attributed proposition becoming a world fact.

support_guard.const: Descriptors are non-exclusive and never upgrade review status. A theorem proves only its exact statement under its assumptions; a primary text establishes what that text says under a declared edition and interpretation, not that its claim is true.

translation_guard.const: A translated term remains indexed by source language, edition, translator, context, school, and interpretive loss; lexical resemblance never establishes shared reference.

rule.const: Replace is, is not, no, and no-no with a typed predicate before drawing a mathematical, historical, metaphysical, or theological inference.
